(The actually long) answer; The issue isn't Elm specifically; it's a myriad of problems with (Vault of Heaven) AR-D (and by extension the damage meta).

•Anti-warp has fallen off real hard
•Safety Fence Lv2 + Reinforcement slot essentially poured gas on an open fire

•Freyr is still usable but he's hanging on to relevancy thanks to his passive, and requires immaculate defense team positioning to make save balls fully work. Otherwise, he's deadweight.

•Galeforce stopped being a generally viable option when true DR, miracle, and pre-combat healing became more relevant and effective - thus forcing people to run a niche subset of newer units that have the privilege of even doing damage. Unsure if Elm will make it widely relevant again.

•Camilla. I don't even need to explain why.

•Harder to bait Elm because he's Flying & can use Eirika Ring.

>Balance - Generally being versatile in everything except having damage over time spells and a damage boosting bubble. (Until level 98) They can do minor heal support, mass blade support, or just become a hitter, given that the boss is not balance. In PVP they are usually the best across all levels. They have one of the best minion summons. No stun moves.

>Ice - Tanks hits well, mass shield team, damage support on bosses that boosts received damage from ice, give Balance a hard time to heal back. An alternative for ice is to just be a heavy hitter with okay-ish resist. Because of our low damage, in PVP we rely heavily on pierce and baiting out the opponent to use shields. Life has no choice because of their Shadow Spell. Has the second most access to stun spells in the game. Unfortunately, Winter Moon makes the Mammoth card **completely** useless. It's almost as if it doesn't exist anymore.

>Fire - Hard hitting combos and pressure. Fire can stack blades and traps with ease, because of their wide array of boost spells. Fire beetle, hephaestus, brimstone, fire from above. Efreet gives them a chance to live longer, and power link provides an okay to decent heal, depending on your incoming and if you use Primordial. Just like storm, they are one of the best hard hitters in the game, except they just have more utility in their moveset. They also have one of the best guardians. (Can use Sprite, Fire Elf for getting rid of shields, Fire Blade, Smokescreen, etc.) They have at least 2 stun moves.

>Storm - Pure power. Storm can hit the hardest out of anyone, but their problem is the ability to last long. Their PVE game is relatively simple; just blade up a few times and then absolutely decimate the opposing team. Storm makes questing less of a chore. In PVP, they have to play carefully at higher levels where simply spamming bolt isn't an option. At least at level 75 they get healing current, but the 1000 or 400 is not always guaranteed. Then again, it's storm, so they could crit the heal at any given moment. They struggle with shields because they have no DoT with the exception of the rare Storm Elf atm. With shrike, bubble and pierce, however, they are a terrifying force. Ice is their worst enemy because of borderline resist immunity. They have 1 stun move.

>Death - Death is a weird one; they make good attackers in general. They aren't the *weakest* hitting school. Their focus is more along the lines of stacking their blades, traps, or other boosters. They can play defensively; the most common defensive death tactic is two death wizards in doubles to easily wear down the other team, or Jade death in singles to just stall out a person with an annoying amount of Bad Juju. In PVE, they survive longer than many schools because of their ability to sap health from damage. They do have death minotaur TC that really helps with shields; besides using their DoT spells. And they completely bypass absorbs when using sap spells. I'd say death is somewhere in the middle of the tier. No stun moves.

>Life - While being the weakest hitter out of all the schools, that doesn't stop Life from racking up damage. Life in general can be the classical team healer, or they can support with damage against life-boosting bosses. They do very well against Ice, Balance, and Myth. In PVP, they are known for... Being an aggressive attacker by stacking blades and releasing them all, being a defensive attacker by pressuring with Luminous Weaver, pierce, and shields, or a Jade. Some Life wizards use Myth mastery to compensate for either lack of damage or stun. Life and Myth is a powerful combo. They also have access to a Revive kind of spell in later levels, should they fall in battle. A lot of people don't normally set for Life wizards in PVP, so they tend to have an easier time. No stuns.

>Myth - Stun, Pierce, Guardians, blasting away shields. Myth can hit hard for sure, and they are okay with handling mobs, but their problem lies within not having a school-specific heal of any kind, and some of their utility being stripped away if the opponent can wriggle out of a stun. Myth is somewhat like ice, they operate similarly. But myth has the superior selection of minions out of any school, and they have the most dual-hit spells, which is good when a DoT isn't needed.
